   <pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 04:49:37 +0200</pubDate>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize</link>
      <description><p>Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</p><p></p><p>The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/sep/16/israel-committed-genocide-in-gaza-says-un-inquiry">that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</a>.</p><p>The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/09/isaias-strengthens-first-atlantic-hurricane-2026</link>
      <description><p>Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding</p><p>Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).</p><p>As a result of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/sep/26/what-is-el-nino-causes-can-we-reduce-risks">the strong El Niño</a>, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/09/isaias-strengthens-first-atlantic-hurricane-2026">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/09/egypt-six-journalists-matsadaash-protest-over-detentions</link>
      <description><p>Matsadaash staff allege torture and forced confessions after being held on charges of working for Muslim Brotherhood</p><p>Egyptian journalists are planning a new protest in Cairo this weekend after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/04/egyptian-journalist-faces-terrorism-charges-entire-newsroom-detained-matsadaash-press-freedom">six colleagues were charged with terrorism offences</a> amid allegations they had been tortured in police detention.</p><p>Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/muslim-brotherhood">Muslim Brotherhood</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/09/egypt-six-journalists-matsadaash-protest-over-detentions">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 01:45:51 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Americas</category><title>'Breaking Bad' actor and disability activist RJ Mitte dies aged 34</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261013-breaking-bad-actor-and-disability-activist-rj-mitte-dies-aged-34</link><description>
"Breaking Bad" actor RJ Mitte, who played Walter White Jr. in the hit US television series, has died aged 34, his representatives said Monday. The actor, who lived with cerebral palsy, also became a prominent disability rights advocate, championing inclusion and representation in film and television.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3ae51ebe-c69e-11f1-8ce7-29a2e29ae696/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25157102255151.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3ae51ebe-c69e-11f1-8ce7-29a2e29ae696/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25157102255151.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6f2ece1e-c6a7-11f1-8abe-a993eb2b6dc5</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 01:43:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3ae51ebe-c69e-11f1-8ce7-29a2e29ae696/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25157102255151.jpg">© Andy Kropa, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>What we know about Pope Leo XIV's planned lung operation this week</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261012-what-we-know-about-pope-leo-xiv-planned-lung-operation-this-week</link><description>
Pope Leo XIV is expected to undergo surgery to remove a lung nodule this week at Rome’s Gemelli hospital, with doctors anticipating a recovery of about seven days. The 71-year-old pontiff is due to travel to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on November 6, though the Vatican has not confirmed the operation date.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2c428f50-bb58-11f1-a1b9-8f3418d01115/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-28T155925Z-496606537-RC2FSNABCLSJ-RTRMADP-3-POPE-FRANCE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2c428f50-bb58-11f1-a1b9-8f3418d01115/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-28T155925Z-496606537-RC2FSNABCLSJ-RTRMADP-3-POPE-FRANCE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">341b2af0-c68b-11f1-be6c-c1e164f0c3a6</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 22:20:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2c428f50-bb58-11f1-a1b9-8f3418d01115/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-28T155925Z-496606537-RC2FSNABCLSJ-RTRMADP-3-POPE-FRANCE.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French supermarkets suffer refrigerator shutdown after 'unprecedented' cyberattack</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/french-supermarkets-suffer-refrigerator-shutdown-after-unprecedented-cyberattack</link><description>
Major French supermarket chains on Monday said they were hit by a cyberattack that caused their refrigerators to shoot up in temperature in hundreds of stores, forcing spoiled food to be thrown away and raising concerns about food security. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/91c2240a-c682-11f1-b3c0-3774aeac812a/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261012-231249-231450-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/91c2240a-c682-11f1-b3c0-3774aeac812a/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261012-231249-231450-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">97811a0e-c682-11f1-a574-93638ea9dad2</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 21:27:53 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Africa</category><title>DR Congo's former president Joseph Kabila to lead new movement with M23 rebels</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20261012-dr-congo-former-president-joseph-kabila-to-lead-new-movement-with-m23-rebels</link><description>
Former DR Congo president Joseph Kabila announced a new political-military alliance with Rwanda-backed M23 rebels on Monday, despite being sentenced to death in absentia for alleged complicity with the group. The move comes as debate grows over constitutional changes ahead of President Felix Tshisekedi’s final term ending in 2028.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7910c4e6-7f90-11f0-99ca-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-48NY9FH.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7910c4e6-7f90-11f0-99ca-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-48NY9FH.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c1a5a36c-c683-11f1-bec4-a1ea1072ad80</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 21:27:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7910c4e6-7f90-11f0-99ca-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-48NY9FH.jpg">© Jospin Mwisha, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Business</category><title>Paris Motor Show kicks off as China-EU rivalry heats up</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/business/20261012-paris-motor-show-kicks-off-as-china-eu-rivalry-heats-up</link><description>
The biennial Paris Motor Show kicks off with a record number of Chinese brands descending on the French capital.  European carmakers are fighting back, showcasing their latest models, as the EU announced a deal with China to limit the imports of hybrids.  France 24's Charles Pellegrin has been speaking with CEOs of both Chinese and European carmakers. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5e7f6e16-c67f-11f1-965c-e362370cce2e/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-14168453346acd4971049550-12762773.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5e7f6e16-c67f-11f1-965c-e362370cce2e/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-14168453346acd4971049550-12762773.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6cfb4bbc-c680-11f1-9b96-ab4b398aec43</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 21:03:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Yuka ROYER</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description>Over the coming weeks, Hong Kong and Shenzhen will host two major gatherings of Asia-Pacific decision-makers. <![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Mon, 12 Oct 2026 21:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ SpaceX launching 6,300 pounds of cargo to the ISS on Oct. 13: Watch it live ]]>

SpaceX will launch its latest cargo mission to the International Space Station on Tuesday morning (Oct. 13), and you can watch the action live.

A Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to launch a robotic Dragon capsule to the orbiting lab from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Tuesday at 6:33 a.m. EDT (1033 GMT).

You can watch the action live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA, starting at 6:15 a.m. EDT (1015 GMT).

The launch will kick off the CRS-35 mission, so named because it will be the 35th that SpaceX flies under a Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

If all goes according to plan, Dragon will reach the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Oct. 15), docking autonomously to the space-facing port of its Harmony module at around 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT). You can watch the arrival here at Space.com as well; coverage will start at 9:15 a.m. EDT (1315 GMT).

CRS-35 will deliver 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays (iROSAs), which will boost the orbiting lab's energy budget.

There's also quite a bit of scientific gear heading up on the flight.

Dragon "will deliver hardware to manufacture artificial retinas in microgravity to help restore vision on Earth and 3D heart tissue models to advance large‑scale drug testing on future missions," NASA officials wrote in a CRS-35 launch preview on Oct. 7.

"The spacecraft will carry materials to study how a new type of glass forms in microgravity and brain organoids that could reveal treatment targets for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and multiple sclerosis," they added.

Dragon will stay attached to the ISS for about a month, then head back down to Earth with scientific experiments and other hardware. It will splash down safely under parachutes in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast.

Dragon is the only currently operational freighter that can carry cargo in the downward direction. The other three — Russia's Progress, Japan's HTV-X and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL — are all expendable, burning up in Earth's atmosphere after their time at the ISS is done.

]]> <![CDATA[ Astronomers witness supermassive black hole gorge on a cosmic meal before 'burping' radio jets 300 days later ]]> Using the NASA X-ray spacecraft Swift combined with radio observations, astronomers have observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal. The team was also able to roughly estimate the mass of this feeding cosmic titan, which sits at the heart of the Perseus Cluster, a massive collection of thousands of galaxies.

The black hole sits at the center of the galaxy NGC 1275, located around 225 light-years away, and is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus Cluster. The supermassive black hole first flared in X-rays, which indicated an increase in the rate at which it was accreting matter. Actively feeding supermassive black holes sit in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs), with their immense gravity heating surrounding matter, causing them to glow brightly. These emissions are boosted by material channeled to the poles of the central black hole, from where it is blasted out as powerful twin jets that shine across the electromagnetic spectrum, particularly in radio waves.

The observation of the following radio jet from the AGN at the heart of NGC 1275 via flaring in radio waves is crucial for understanding the relationship between the disk of matter that surrounds and feeds the black hole, called an accretion disk, and the jets it launches. This so-called disk-jet coupling is key to developing a better picture of how black holes influence star formation in the galaxies in which they sit, and thus the growth of those galaxies.

Making these observations is no mean feat. The ideal spacecraft for observing X-ray emissions is Chandra, but it doesn't observe NGC 1275 frequently enough to observe its long-term behaviour. NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory may lack the power of Chandra, but having launched in 2004, it has collected a vast amount of data regarding NGC 1275 and its central supermassive black hole.

"It is fairly difficult to see the inner region of this AGN because NGC 1275 is at the center of the massive Perseus cluster of galaxies, which adds additional light to our observations," team leader Sarah Ketchum of the University of Michigan told Space.com. "We developed a model that allowed us to remove the cluster emission from archival Swift data, and in doing so, we were able to see the changes in the X-ray flux from gas accreting onto the black hole in NGC 1275, from 2007 to 2025."

Ketchum added that the capabilities of Swift were key to this investigation of NGC 1275, which is the ideal laboratory for the study of disk-jet coupling.

"There have been studies on other galaxies with AGN that show evidence of coupling between gas accretion traced in X-ray light and gas ejection in jets, traced in radio light. But NGC 1275 reveals the impact of black hole jets on large spatial scales better than any other system," the University of Michigan researcher continued.

This black hole didn't eat a star

Ketchum and colleagues saw the strongest ever X-ray flare from NGC 1275 in Feb. 2023. Lasting less than 60 days and consisting of two 5-day blasts, this episode saw a doubling of the X-ray brightness of the AGN at the heart of NGC 1275.

The flaring was so extreme that the team had to rule out a tidal disruption event (TDE) as the cause. These occur when an unfortunate star's orbit brings it too close to the immense gravitational influence of a supermassive black hole. This influence generates intense tidal forces that simultaneously squash and squeeze the star, "speghettifying" it and allowing the black hole to snack on some plasma pasta.

"We were able to rule out TDEs as a cause," Ketchum said. "Thus, the flaring was likely caused by a spike in the rate at which matter accreted onto the black hole."

Using Swift data, the team was able to infer the radius over which the AGN emits radiation. Because the size of a black hole is directly correlated with its mass, this meant that the researchers were able to constrain the mass of the black hole at the heart of NGC 1275. They determined that this supermassive black hole has a mass somewhere between 100 million times the mass of the sun and 1 billion solar masses.

The team then compared their data to known radio data to better understand the relationship between the X-ray emission and the radio jets that disrupt gas in NGC 1275.

Ketchum added that she and her colleagues found tentative evidence of around a 300-day delay between the X-ray flaring and the radio wave emission. This indicates the time it takes plasma to travel from the base of the jet to a knot or shock created when it hits surrounding gas or dust.

"This should be tested further in the future. Our X-ray data only sparsely sample the changes in NGC 1275," Ketchum said. "This makes it difficult to determine an exact relationship between the X-ray and radio radiation for large portions of our light curve, so we would need more X-ray data to further study this connection."

The researcher added that if the X-ray flares are produced close to the black hole, an echo of these flares should be seen coming from the accretion disk.

"An emission line from neutral iron is seen in data from NGC 1275, and this may be the echo. However, we likely need many observations with XMM-Newton and XRISM ( X-Ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission) to really establish that connection," Ketchum concluded.

The team's research has been accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal Letters, with a pre-peer-review version available on the repository site arXiv.

The team's research has been accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal Letters, with a pre-peer-review version available on the repository site arXiv.

]]> <![CDATA[ The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft ]]> NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.

The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here.

NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits. "This problem is severely compounded when entering lunar shadows and permanently shadowed regions," the agency wrote, referring to deeply cratered areas where the sun does not touch the lunar surface.

The concern is that astronauts' spacesuits could become electrically charged, as there would be an excess of electrons (negatively charged particles) compared with ions (positively charged) in these areas.

"The risk occurs when an astronaut returns to the spacecraft," the agency added. The lander would have a slight positive charge, producing an issue once the "highly negatively-charged astronaut approaches the vehicle."

NASA has asked industry partners for ideas that can help an astronaut avoid "becoming a walking, high voltage capacitor", including issues such as an electrical arc that could damage spacesuits, spark fires in the oxygen atmosphere of a spacecraft, or create electrical shocks. (A Mars simulation in 2018 was reportedly derailed due to a crew experiencing electrical issues, so this problem is not unprecedented.)

The challenge aims to create designs that would safely discharge the astronaut and their spacesuit before an astronaut touches the lander. Among the technical requirements, NASA is looking for something small (in terms of mass, volume and power) that would be able to operate even in the extreme temperature swings of the lunar surface. The technology must also be able to help as many as four extra-vehicular activities (moonwalks) that take place over as long as 10 days.

"In addition, the suspended lunar dust and heavy dust buildup on a suit in these environments significantly increases arcing lengths, allowing sparks to jump across larger gaps than they would in a clean vacuum. Therefore, the solution must aim to avoid a sudden arc that may come into contact with the outer pressure garment — suit — or the lander," NASA wrote in the challenge description.

The challenge will include multiple phases, including a concept design, concept refinement after chatting with reviewers, and then a final selection. NASA did not release a target date in its press release for when the tech would be available for astronauts, but the agency is planning on a long-term moon base for astronaut missions that would be largely ready to go in the 2030s if schedules hold.

]]> <![CDATA[ The 'Halloween Fireballs' are coming. Here's what to expect from the Taurids this year ]]> They don't produce anything like the torrent of "shooting stars" associated with August's Perseids or December's Geminids, but the Taurid meteor showers have something else going for them — fireballs.

The Taurids are famous for occasionally producing exceptionally bright, slow-moving meteors that can streak dramatically across the night sky from September to December. As a bonus, they're visible from both the Northern and Southern hemispheres. That's because they appear to emanate from the constellation Taurus, which sits close to the ecliptic, the apparent path the sun takes across the sky as Earth orbits around it.

The Taurids are actually two closely related showers — the Southern Taurids and Northern Taurids — whose activity overlaps in late October and November. That's why they're known informally by skywatchers as the "Halloween fireballs." The broad overlapping peaks make the Taurids less about watching on one particular night and more about keeping an eye on the night sky for several weeks. Both have their radiant points — the place in the night sky where their "shooting stars" appear to come from — close to the famous Pleiades (M45) open cluster of stars in the constellation Taurus.

There's another tempting reason to watch the Taurids in 2026 — moonlight will cause little interference around the main peaks.

When are the Southern Taurids?

The Southern Taurids are already underway. According to the American Meteor Society, they're active from Sept. 20 through Nov. 20, with two distinct components. The annual component peaks around Oct. 14, while a component particularly associated with fireballs peaks overnight on Nov. 4-5. That's the night to circle if you're hoping to see one of the "Halloween Fireballs."

However, don't expect a conventional meteor storm. The Southern Taurids have an average zenithal hourly rate of about five meteors per hour. ZHR describes how many meteors an observer could theoretically see under ideal conditions with the shower's radiant directly overhead. In practice, observers see fewer, so this is not a chance to gather friends for a special show, as with the Perseids.

What the Southern Taurids lack in quantity, however, they can make up for in quality. Their meteors strike Earth's atmosphere at about 17 miles (27 kilometers) per second. That's relatively slow for a meteor, helping make some Taurids conspicuous as they travel across the sky. You don't see a Taurid meteor; you watch it.

If clouds allow, conditions should be favorable around Nov. 4-5. The moon will be absent most of the night, rising a couple of hours before dawn as a 17%-illuminated waning crescent — too dim to affect visibility of meteors.

When are the Northern Taurids?

The Northern Taurids begin later, becoming active on Oct. 20 and continuing through Dec. 10, according to the American Meteor Society. They're expected to peak overnight on Nov. 11-12.

Once again, rates are low — around five meteors per hour under ideal conditions — but fireballs are possible. Northern Taurid meteors enter the atmosphere at around 18 miles (29 km) per second, similarly as slow as their southern counterparts.

Observing conditions at the peak should be excellent. The moon will be a slender 5%-illuminated waxing crescent and will be practically absent from the night sky overnight on Nov. 11-12, leaving the night dark.

The distinction between the two Taurid showers isn't particularly important if you're simply outside hoping to see a fireball. In late October and early November, both streams are active at the same time, potentially producing around 10 Taurids per hour under clear, moon-free conditions.

Why are Taurids called the 'Halloween Fireballs'?

The nickname comes partly from timing. Their maxima are also broad rather than sharp. According to EarthSky, the Taurids tend to "ramble along" over the period, becoming particularly noticeable when the two branches overlap from late October into early November — Halloween.

It's also a reference to their tendency to produce fireballs, exceptionally bright meteors caused when larger pieces of space debris plunge into Earth's atmosphere.

Some years are considerably better for Taurid fireballs than others, and it's impossible to tell for sure in advance. EarthSky notes that enhanced displays occurred in 2008, 2015 and 2022, when Earth encountered concentrations of larger debris within the stream. However, don't expect a repeat in 2026 — the next predicted Taurid fireball swarm isn't expected until 2032.

That doesn't mean there won't be fireballs this year, only that an unusually high number isn't predicted.

What causes the Taurid meteor showers?

Both Taurid meteor showers are linked to Comet 2P/Encke, a three-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) comet that circles the sun every 3.25 years — the shortest known cometary orbit, according to NASA. However, the Taurids belong to a much larger complex of dust, rocks, comets and asteroids, possibly created when a much bigger object fragmented thousands of years ago. Each fall, Earth crosses different parts of this sprawling debris stream, producing the overlapping Northern and Southern Taurids and, occasionally, the larger fragments that create spectacular fireballs.

How to see the Taurid meteor showers

Both showers appear to originate from Taurus, a constellation that rises during the evening and climbs higher into the sky as the night progresses. Around midnight, Taurus is well placed for many observers.

However, there's no need to find Taurus. Meteors can appear anywhere in the sky, and staring directly at the radiant can actually mean seeing shorter meteor trails. The best advice is to treat the period as a great time for naked-eye stargazing, with the usual rules applying — find somewhere away from bright lights with as wide a view of the sky as possible, and give your eyes about 20 minutes to adjust to the darkness. Binoculars and telescopes will restrict your field of view and make meteor watching impossible.

Above all, be patient. The Taurids are a slow burn in every sense — low rates, slow-moving meteors and weeks of activity. But if one of those meteors happens to be a brilliant fireball, it could easily be one of the most memorable "shooting stars" you see all year.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 12, 1964: The Soviet Union launches Voskhod 1, the 1st multi-person cosmonaut crew, into space ]]>

On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, a 24-hour crewed mission that achieved several "firsts" for human spaceflight. This was the first time that a spacecraft carried more than one person into orbit, with three cosmonauts packed inside the spacecraft.

Only two cosmonauts were originally supposed to fly on this mission, but Soviet politicians pressured the Russian space program to add one more. This left no room for spacesuits on board, so this also became the first spaceflight without spacesuits.

Two of the crewmembers, an engineer and a doctor, became the first civilians to go to space.

Why it mattered

Voskhod 1 served as yet another first for the Soviet Union during a space race kicked off by the launch of Sputnik 1 in 1957 and followed up by the first human spaceflight with Yuri Gagarin in 1961. And while the United States did follow up with its one human spaceflights, until Oct. 12, 1964, every mission had one person on board.

That changed with Voskhod 1, which crammed three man into a spacecraft not much larger than the Soviet Union's one-person Vostok spacecraft. At the time, NASA was develoing the two-person Gemini spacecraft, which prompted the Soviet Union's then leader to push for an edge.

"Soviet leader [Nikita] Khrushchev contacted Korolev and ordered him to convert the Vostok spacecraft into a vehicle capable of carrying not two, but three cosmonauts," according to space historian Asif Siddiqi, referring to Sergei Korolev, chief designer of the Soviet space program.

In order to fit a three people inside, the Voskhod 1 cosmonauts - commander Vladimir Komarov and his crew Konstantin Feoktistov and Boris Yegorov - did not wear spacesuits traditionally used for launch and landing, adding substantial risk to the flight. They also stayed inside their spacecraft when it landed, unlike Vostok crews like Gagarin, who parachuted out of them after reentry.

The Voskhod 1 mission lasted just over 24 hours, during which its crew performed experimented with the behavior of liquids and gases in microgravity and photographed the Earth.

NASA's first multi-crew mission, Gemini 3, would launch about six month later on March 23, 1965.

]]> <![CDATA[ Namibian salt flats look like an alien planet | Space photo of the day for Oct. 12, 2026 ]]>

A neon blue pool swirls amongst what look like clouds, all surrounded by a bright red stretch of land. This might look like the surface of an alien planet, but it's actually a salt flat right here on Earth, seen from space.

What is it?

Etosha National Park in northern Namibia hosts the largest salt pan, or piece of land covered with salt and other minerals, in the country.

This image of the Etosha Pan was captured on April 5 of this year by Europe's Copernicus Sentinel-2 mission, which consists of two identical satellites in the same orbit.

The Sentinel-2 pair observe and capture imagery of our planet in different wavelengths using a high-resolution multispectral imager that can see 13 different spectral bands, or ranges of wavelengths.

By looking at our planet from space, and observing it through different wavelengths and colors, we can better understand Earth's topography and how it changes over time. With this image, researchers can better understand this landmark in Namibia, a nation in southwestern Africa.

Why is it incredible?

While this image is strikingly beautiful, the Etosha Pan doesn't exactly look like this in real life. If you were standing close to the pan in the national park, it would look bright white.

While this is a real image, false color has been added, which allows scientists to separate different types of vegetation and topography.

With the false color, the vegetation surrounding the salt pan appears in shades of red, while the salt pan itself looks like a mix of bright, light and dark blues with cloudy sediment floating around.

The varied vegetation captured in this false-color image includes grassland, savannas and mopane trees, which appear bright red. These trees are not only a dominant type of vegetation in areas of this park, they also provide essential shelter and habitats for local wildlife, including elephants, giraffe and leopards.

]]> <![CDATA[ How the impossible geometry of 'Tomb Raider III''s UFO level was made ]]> "Tomb Raider" celebrates its 30th anniversary this month. While many remember the iconic T-Rex or locking Winston the Butler in the freezer, many forget about the UFO in 1998’s "Tomb Raider III"; a mysterious alien craft that worked a lot like Doctor Who’s TARDIS.

Coming off the back of the hugely successful "Tomb Raider 2", developer Core Design had big plans for the third entry, including kayaking, those iconic London levels, and, of course, a level featuring a UFO in Area 51. Although it looked small on the outside, the UFO featured multiple floors for players to explore as they searched for a vital artifact, all as enemies swarmed in.

Now, I'm something of a Tomb Raider historian, and my upcoming book — "The Making of Tomb Raider: 1997-2000" (available from October 30) — goes into detail about the making of "Tomb Raider III", "Tomb Raider IV", and other games in the series during those three years. While writing the book, I spoke to level designer Richard Morton about how the physics-defying UFO was made and how shows like "The X-Files" inspired him and the team.

The Lone Gunwoman

When you start "Tomb Raider III", you find Lara in India, stumbling across one of four artifacts. After completing India, you can choose between London, South Pacific, and Nevada to collect the other artifacts before reaching the final section in Antarctica.

Richard Morton was one of the designers for "Tomb Raider III", who took on South Pacific and some of Nevada, a location that Neal Boyd had already begun work on before he moved to "Project Eden". Eventually, Lara would find herself in Area 51, with the final part of the level taking place in a UFO that houses the artifact she seeks.

“Area 51 was a bit of a team effort,” reveals Morton. “The part where the rocket launches, Neal did a lot of that stuff. So much of that level is his work, as well as some of the other routes. Andy Sandham helped in finishing off that level, too. And then the bit with the UFO, that was mine.”

Of course, a level called Area 51 needed aliens. In the late 1990s, UFOs were everywhere, ranging from TV shows like The X-Files to countless documentaries on whether aliens were real.

“We knew Area 51 had to have aliens in it in some form. And we did put some down on operating tables – we were all influenced by films and shows like 'The X-Files' and 'Independence Day', which were around at the time of TR3.”

You’d run past the UFO at certain points in between toggling switches, collecting keys, and even launching a rocket. Eventually, you’d unlock a door, letting you in to reveal an impossibly large interior. But all wasn’t as it seemed, and the journey to get here was fraught with challenges.

“I was working quite late one evening, and it wasn't a UFO to start with. ]]> <![CDATA[ What caused a mysterious atmospheric explosion in Siberia in 1908? ]]> Fire erupted in the morning skies over Siberia on June 30, 1908, as an atmospheric explosion occurred that remains unmatched by any similar event in modern history.

That day, at approximately 7:15 a.m. local time, observers in Siberia's remote Tunguska region became witnesses to the entry of a brilliant fireball into Earth's atmosphere, trailing smoke across the dawn sky and culminating in a flash brighter than the sun itself. Within seconds, the explosion and resulting shock waves that followed reportedly knocked some members of the nearby Indigenous Evenki population off their feet, and caused damage to dwellings and livestock, while seismic instruments hundreds of miles away logged tremors caused by the blast.

The blast produced enough energy to flatten a significant stretch of the Siberian wilderness, marking an event that still serves as a cautionary tale — and a major point of reference — for modern planetary defense efforts. Yet some questions remain about exactly what happened, and what the implications are for future potential Tunguska-scale events. For many years after the events of that day, the cause of the blast — known today as the Tunguska event — remained unknown. With time, a likely culprit emerged: scientists now believe a small asteroid, estimated to have been just 130 feet (40 meters) in diameter, exploded after entering Earth's atmosphere.

What do we know?

Unraveling the Tunguska Event mystery

Remarkably, scientists wouldn't get a firsthand look at the destruction caused by the Tunguska blast for almost two decades, due primarily to the extreme remoteness of the blast location. Further complicating scientific investigations were the First World War, the Russian Revolution, and the ensuing civil war.

One of the earliest attempts to reach the blast site was initiated in 1921 by Soviet geologist Leonid Kulik, who failed in his first effort, but did eventually make his way to Tunguska six years later. Upon arriving, the devastation caused by the event was unmistakable even after nearly two decades.

Curiously, at the blast site's presumed epicenter, a small area of unaffected trees remained standing, albeit stripped of some of their bark and branches. The surrounding countryside, by comparison, was littered with large numbers of trees that were toppled as the shock waves produced by the exploding asteroid high above radiated downward.

In the decades that followed, additional assessment of the site that included expeditions and aerial surveys, primarily during the 1950s and 1960s, revealed another curious feature: a distinctive hourglass- or butterfly-shaped destruction zone spanning well over 800 square miles (2,070 square kilometers), with millions of trees estimated to have been flattened. Yet most curious of all had been what investigators did not find; despite a blast zone of this size, there was no evidence of an impact crater at Tunguska.

An airburst over Siberia

What the evidence seemed to suggest was that an explosion had occurred not on the surface following a massive impact, but instead high in Earth's atmosphere — probably as much as several miles above the Earth — as tremendous aerodynamic stresses caused the object to fragment and release its energy before reaching the ground.

A longstanding debate about the Tunguska object has centered on whether it was more likely an asteroid or a comet, although today, most evidence appears to favor an asteroid. Among the clues supporting an asteroid origin are mineral and chemical signatures identified in material collected from the region that researchers have argued are consistent with a stony or carbonaceous asteroid. However, identifying physical remnants definitively associated with the Tunguska object has remained challenging.

What remains unknown?

A warning from the sky?

While the Tunguska event remains an enigma in some ways, it also offers modern researchers an opportunity to study one of the rare recent examples in Earth's geological history of a large-scale cosmic airburst.

Deeper in Earth's past — around 66 million years ago — a six-mile-wide (10 km) asteroid struck what is now Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula. The impact created the 120-mile-wide (190 km) Chicxulub crater in a cataclysmic event that drove mass extinctions across the planet, eliminating nearly three-quarters of the species that thrived on Earth until that time.

Of course, even objects orders of magnitude smaller than the object that created the Chicxulub crater can pose a danger to Earth. Although the object that struck Earth 66 million years ago is believed to have been as much as 200 times wider and millions of times more massive than the suspected asteroid that exploded over Siberia in 1908, estimates indicate that a Tunguska-scale event would be capable of killing millions if it occurred today over a city the size of New York.

Such estimates aren't based entirely on theory, either. In February 2013, planetary scientists were given a dramatic opportunity to gauge the effects of such an event when a previously undetected 60-foot-wide (20 meters) asteroid exploded after entering Earth's atmosphere over Chelyabinsk, Russia.

The resulting blast, which released energy equivalent to an estimated 500 kilotons of TNT, was captured on cameras throughout the region as it damaged buildings and caused injuries to more than 1,000 people, mostly due to flying glass from windows that were shattered by the blast wave.

A wake-up call for planetary defense

Because of events like Chelyabinsk and Tunguska, planetary scientists have worked to expand initiatives that detect and monitor potentially hazardous near-Earth objects (NEOs) that could become a concern in the decades ahead.

Still, despite such efforts having been in effect at the time, the Chelyabinsk event represented an example of a potentially dangerous NEO that effectively managed to sneak up on us. Fortunately, despite the damage that was caused, things could have been far worse. But will we be so lucky next time?

To help mitigate such concerns, in 2016 NASA established the Planetary Defense Coordination Office to help align its efforts with those of its international partners and develop more advanced methods of identifying and tracking any NEOs that could pose an impact threat.

Then in 2022, NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) demonstrated the use of a spacecraft as a kinetic impactor, which was intentionally sent on a collision course with Dimorphos, the small moon of the asteroid Didymos, which altered Dimorphos' orbital period around its companion by approximately 33 minutes. Such technology could one day prove to be vital if another potential Tunguska-type object were found to be on a collision course with Earth.

The mystery continues

Fact, fiction, and planning for the future

Given the questions that remain about Tunguska, as well as the misrepresentations and persistent myths surrounding it, several scientists have also worked in recent years to combat misinformation about the 1908 event.

In a paper published in March 2026 in the journal Meteoritics & Planetary Science, authors Mark Boslough and colleagues noted that future planning for evacuation plans and other mitigation efforts "depend critically on our ability to model these events, which depends on our understanding of the governing physics, which in turn is validated by sparse data on real events such as Tunguska."

"If people do not have confidence in the models on which evacuation plans are based, they could lose their lives," the study's authors warned.

More than a century after it occurred, June 30 is now recognized as International Asteroid Day, commemorating not only the blast's anniversary, but also the need for awareness of the dangerous potential future similar events could present.

Tunguska therefore remains a source of fascination for scientists, as well as an opportunity to better understand — and to prepare for — any potential future threats posed by similar objects, should one eventually be found on a collision course with Earth.

]]> <![CDATA[ UAE unveils lander for bold 7-asteroid mission set to launch in 2028 (photos) ]]> The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has moved a step closer to launching its second-ever interplanetary mission — an ambitious, eight-year exploration of seven asteroids between Mars and Jupiter that will culminate with a landing on the mysteriously red asteroid 269 Justitia.

The mission team unveiled a half-scale model of the homegrown probe that will make that landing during an Oct. 1 press conference in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE. The autonomous craft will ride attached to the main spacecraft MBR Explorer, named after Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, the ruler of Dubai and the UAE's prime minister.

The flight-ready lander is being kept pristine in a vacuum chamber in the capital before being transported to Colorado by Etihad Airways, officials said, where it will be integrated with the main spacecraft, which was developed by the UAE Space Agency.

If all goes to plan, the mission will lift off from Japan in March 2028, kicking off the Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA). The project is an ambitious follow-up to the UAE Space Agency's Hope Mars orbiter, which has been studying the Red Planet since 2021.

"It's a proud moment for us here at the UAE," said Faisal al-Bannai, the secretary general of the Advanced Technology Research Council in Abu Dhabi.

'We don't know what we're going to find'

EMA will conduct high-speed flybys of six asteroids before reaching and orbiting 269 Justitia. It will travel a total of about 3 billion miles (5 billion kilometers), which is equivalent to circling Earth roughly 125,000 times, said Najwa Aaraj, the CEO of the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in Abu Dhabi, which designed, built and tested the mission's lander.

Along the way, the MBR Explorer will utilize gravity assists from Venus and then Earth to swing deeper into space, zipping past its first three asteroid targets: 10253 Westerwald, 623 Chimaera and 13294 Rockox. A subsequent gravity assist from Mars will fling the spacecraft even farther out, guiding it past three more space rocks: 88055 Ghaf, 23871 Ousha and 59980 Moza.

By 2036, the spacecraft is scheduled to rendezvous with its final and most intriguing target, 269 Justitia. A roughly 30-mile-wide (50 km) object in the middle of the asteroid belt, 269 Justitia is unusual for its remarkably crimson hue.

Its distinct color more closely resembles icy objects in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune than its immediate main-belt neighbors. This unique trait has led planetary scientists to hypothesize that the asteroid formed in the frigid outer solar system and migrated inward early in the solar system's history. If true, visiting 269 Justitia would offer a rare, close-up look at pristine material from the distant outer solar system via a much shorter journey.

Scientists are particularly excited that the asteroid may still hold water-related minerals and organic compounds preserved from its origins. Studying its surface could therefore offer clues to how water and organic material were distributed as planets began to form, Elias Tsoutsanis, a chief researcher at TII's propulsion and space research center, said during the press briefing.

"We don't know what we're going to find — that's exploration," Tsoutsanis told reporters. "We're really excited."

According to the mission plan, the MBR Explorer will spend roughly seven months studying 269 Justitia from orbit. Beginning at an altitude of 155 miles (250 km), the spacecraft will gradually lower its path before releasing the lander. The smaller probe will then head toward the asteroid's surface, a descent that should take two to three hours depending on 269 Justitia's precise gravity, which remains unknown.

Although TII describes the mission ending with a landing on the surface of 269 Justitia, the engineering details suggest a more violent endgame. Cruising toward the asteroid's surface at 15 to 27 meters per second (34 to 60 mph) with no meaningful way to slow down, the probe will function less like a traditional lander and more like a planned impactor.

"We don't expect that the probe will survive the touchdown," said Mariam Alhammadi, a researcher in TII leading the mission's electric propulsion.

To ensure its two onboard cameras capture essential imagery during the descent, the probe will rely on an attitude-control system to counteract any post-separation spin, Alhammadi said. Should the probe unexpectedly survive the hard landing, she added, its battery is built to last 20 to 50 minutes, providing a narrow but crucial window for it to beam close-ups of the asteroid's surface back to Earth.

The high-velocity impact is also expected to dig a small crater on 269 Justitia, possibly exposing pristine subsurface material. Because this material cannot be imaged from orbit, the team expects the probe's final images to be among the most valuable of the entire mission.

Zero margin for error

Back on Earth, the team faces an unforgiving timeline. To execute the planned flybys, the mission must launch during a narrow three-week window that opens in early March 2028.

"God forbid we miss that — we basically don't have a mission," Mohsen al-Awadhi, the mission director at the UAE Space Agency, told reporters at the press conference. The orbital mechanics are so rigid that another comparable opportunity will not arise for at least 100 years, prompting al-Awadhi to add that he is devoting no time and energy to a backup plan.

Meeting the launch window is just the first hurdle, however. Once deployed in deep space, the lander must operate with absolute autonomy, receiving no commands from Earth or the main MBR Explorer spacecraft, the team says.

"In these eight years, I have no control to call it back — so nothing can go wrong," said Aaraj.

Equipped with AI, it is designed to decide on its own when to capture images and how to filter and rank the most valuable data. Oct. 11, 1968, Apollo 7 launched into space with NASA astronauts Wally Schirra, Donn Eisele and Walter Cunningham. This was the first mission of the Apollo program that carried a crew into space.

Apollo 7 rebooted the Apollo program after a fire killed three astronauts during a launch rehearsal 20 months earlier.

NASA needed to prove that their Apollo spacecraft worked with this mission, which was really more of a test flight. Though the spacecraft seemed to work alright, the crew got a little snippy during their 11 days in space. First they suffered from motion sickness after launch, then Schirra came down with a cold, and the crew was constantly arguing with mission control and each other. None of the Apollo 7 astronauts went back to space after that.

Why it mattered

Had Apollo 7 not succeeded, the chances of NASA being able to fulfill President John F. Kennedy's 1961 goal, "before this decade is out, of landing a man on the moon and returning him safely to the Earth" would be called into question — not just because the clock was ticking down, but because of increasing political pressure to shut down the expensive moon program.

In the wake of the January 1967 Apollo 1 fire, NASA and North American Aviation, the prime contractor for the Apollo command module, needed to overhaul the spacecraft to make it safe for crews to fly in space. Apollo 7 provided a "shakedown cruise" for the vehicle, to confirm the fixes worked and that the command module was space worthy.

"In its day, the Apollo command module was the most complex machine ever built by man to be operated by man," said Walt Cunningham, Apollo 7 pilot, on the 40th anniversary of the flight in 2008. "We launched on the longest and most ambitious engineering test flight in history, testing the spacecraft systems, verifying the operating procedures, checking out the worldwide tracking network, and that's not to mention testing our crew."

Apollo 7 was deemed by NASA to a 101% success, setting up the first lunar landing in July 1969.

"All of us in the flights that followed were dependent on the Apollo 7 crew doing their job," said Neil Armstrong, Apollo 11 commander. "So thanks Walt and Wally and Donn."

  <item>
   <title>Muž, u něhož začala kauza metanol: Stát věděl o pančování lihu léta, říká</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/krimi/metanolova-kauza-stat-o-pancovani-lihu-martin-svoboda-majitel-stanku/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=krimi</link>
   <description>Tuctový prodejní stánek Martina Svobody v Havířově-Šumbarku byl na začátku září 2012 prvním místem v České republice, kde úřady zjistily vůbec první vzorky jedovatého alkoholu. Po vypití lihovin z něj zemřeli čtyři lidé a jeden muž oslepl. Úmrtí stála na počátku bezprecedentní série otrav alkoholem, která je dodnes známá jako metanolová aféra. Zemřelo při ní 51 lidí a dalších asi 120 až 140 se pančovaným alkoholem otrávilo. Většina z nich si nese doživotní následky.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Kvůli salmonelóze v kuřecím mase se zvyšují kontroly. V Česku se na nemoc umírá</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/cesko-zdravi-salmoneloza-kureci-maso-inspekce/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Státní zemědělská a potravinářská inspekce varovala před kuřecím masem ve dvou šaržích, které prodával řetězec Lidl. Šlo o výrobky z Rumunska a Maďarska. Státní veterinární správa ale upozornila, že nejde o ojedinělý případ. Od letošního léta zintenzivnila kvůli salmonelóze kontroly kuřecího masa a přítomnost zdraví ohrožujících látek našla téměř ve čtvrtině testovaných vzorků. V posledních osmi letech zemřela na salmonelózu více než stovka Čechů. Kromě masa se bakterie vyskytují třeba i v koření.</description>
   <pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:05:50 +0200</pubDate>

  <item>
   <title>V kraji volilo víc lidí než před čtyřmi lety. Nejméně jich přišlo na Českolipsku</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/komunalni-volby/v-kraji-volilo-vic-lidi-nez-pred-ctyrmi-lety-nejmene-jich-prislo-na-ceskolipsku/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=komunalni-volby</link>
   <description>V Libereckém kraji přišlo v pátek a v sobotu ke komunálním volbám o 7215 lidí víc než před čtyřmi lety. Volební komise vydaly obálky 158 389 voličům, účast tak dosáhla 46 procent. V roce 2018 hlasovalo v řádném termínu do obecních zastupitelstev 151 174 lidí a účast dosáhla 43,87 procenta. </description>

   <title>Meteorologové změnili předpověď. Mrazy vystřídá oteplení, bude až 20 stupňů</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/pocasi/predpoved-pocasi-cesko-kraje-radar-zima-dest-otepleni/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=pocasi</link>
   <description>Duben je sice dávno za námi, ale počasí v tomto týdnu bude víc než podzim připomínat právě apríl. V pondělí jsme se probudili do chladného rána, na mnoha místech klesly teploty k mrazivým hodnotám a na horách se objevily i sněhové vločky. Začne se ale rychle oteplovat a ke konci pracovního týdne vyskočí teploty až ke dvaceti stupňům. Na víkend však teploty opětovně klesnou.</description>

      <description>Začalo to poklidným a docela nenápadným protestem. Žáci lycea Saint-Exupéryho v Créteil, jihovýchodním předměstí Paříže, představili 21. září soupis svých stížností. <link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/v-radu-mesicu-by-v-cesku-mohl-zacit-fungovat-novy-ai-system-pro-soudce-budou-s-nim-tvorit-rozsudky/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Soudci by si mohli v řádu měsíců začít pomáhat systémem iSoud, projektem s umělou inteligencí, který jim bude pomáhat vytvářet podklady pro jejich rozhodnutí. Hovořil o něm místopředseda pražského vrchního soudu Roman Horáček na konferenci AI v justici. Věří, že výsledkem bude vy&#353;&#353;í kvalita rozhodování. Soudci podle něj získají více času na zpracování a dal&#353;í dohledávání judikatury.</description>

<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/vodafone-s-ceskym-technologickym-talentem-spousti-ochranu-proti-ai-podvodum/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Vodafone spustí slíbenou aplikaci, která pomáhá odhalovat fotografie, videa, hlasové zprávy a dokumenty zmanipulované umělou inteligencí. Na technologii spolupracoval s českým startupem Synhawk, za nímž stojí Maty Boháček, významný český technologický talent, výzkumník AI a deepfake technologií na Stanfordově univerzitě. Služba Vodafone Verify má pomáhat lidem i firmám ověřit podezřelý obsah dříve, než podle něj po&#353;lou peníze nebo udělají jiné důležité rozhodnutí.</description>

<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/nejhodnotnejsi-firma-sveta-nasadila-ceskou-technologii-nvidii-pomaha-trenovat-roboty-budoucnosti/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Americká společnost Nvidia, která je aktuálně díky nástupu AI nejhodnotněj&#353;ím podnikem na světě, začala používat českou technologii vyvinutou v akademickém prostředí, respektive na Matematicko-fyzikální fakultě Univerzity Karlovy. Používá ji pro přípravu dat na trénování modelů umělé inteligence pro autonomní robotiku. Právě roboti schopní samostatného fungování mají být pro Nvidii dal&#353;í velkou oblastí rozvoje (projekty jako GR00T, Jetson a dal&#353;í).</description>

Kudy z nudy – Žebříčky: Liberecký kraj Žebříčky RSS Feed <![CDATA[Šťastné a křišťálové – Vánoce naruby]]>

Přijďte prožít advent do libereckého Paláce Liebieg, kde se letos potkají tradice, kreativita a vánoční atmosféra Křišťálového údolí. Čeká vás jedinečná výstava, která vás zavede do světa fantazie, kde nic není takové, jak se na první pohled zdá.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 15:54:49 GMT <![CDATA[Židovská modlitebna a synagoga Liberec]]>

Novodobá liberecká synagoga je součástí Krajské vědecké knihovny, známé jako Stavba smíření. Otevřena byla roku 2000 na místě synagogy vypálené nacisty. Trojúhelníkový půdorys připomíná část Davidovy hvězdy a interiér uchovává památky původního svatostánku.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:36:28 GMT <![CDATA[Kostel sv. Vojtěcha v Liberci]]>

Kostel sv. Vojtěcha v libereckém Ostašově stojí na místě dřevěné kaple vybudované z odškodnění za sedmiletou válku. Zděná stavba vznikla v letech 1832–1833. Díky péči Spolku přátel Ostašova dnes ožívá koncerty a dalšími kulturními akcemi.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:29:30 GMT <![CDATA[Kostel sv. Jana Křtitele v Liberci]]>

Barokní kostel sv. Jana Křtitele v liberecké Rochlici stojí na místě někdejšího dřevěného evangelického kostela. Zaujme dochovaným historickým vybavením, hlavním oltářem s obrazem patrona chrámu, vyřezávanou kazatelnou a varhanami z roku 1887.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:23:32 GMT

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>Dvě nedělní nehody na Jablonecku: Zatáčky vynesly řidiče do patníku i protisměru</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902804-dve-nedelni-nehody-na-jablonecku-zatacky-vynesly-ridice-do-patniku-i-protismeru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902804-dve-nedelni-nehody-na-jablonecku-zatacky-vynesly-ridice-do-patniku-i-protismeru.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 19:28:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Neděle na Jablonecku se neobešla bez nehod na silnicích. Dva řidiči doplatili na neopatrnost v levotočivých zatáčkách – jeden skončil v protisměru a způsobil zranění druhého šoféra, další se svým vozem narazil čelně do kamenného patníku. Alkohol byl u obou vyloučen.</description></item><item><title>Příprava na zimu na Ještědu začíná: Unikátní technologie chrlí tuny ledu denně</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902811-priprava-na-zimu-na-jestedu-zacina-unikatni-technologie-chrli-tuny-ledu-denne.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902811-priprava-na-zimu-na-jestedu-zacina-unikatni-technologie-chrli-tuny-ledu-denne.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 18:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Skiareál Ještěd se intenzivně připravuje na zimní sezónu a znovu sází na technologii Snow Factory. Ta dokáže vyrobit až 96 tun ledu denně zcela bez ohledu na venkovní teplotu. Unikátní metoda bez použití chemie vytvoří pevný základ na kritických úsecích sjezdovek a výrazně urychlí zahájení lyžování.</description></item><item><title>Proč nesmí děti cestovat v bundě? Tohle se stane při nehodě</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902440-proc-nesmi-deti-cestovat-v-bunde-tohle-se-stane-pri-nehode.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902440-proc-nesmi-deti-cestovat-v-bunde-tohle-se-stane-pri-nehode.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:41:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>Péřovka v autosedačce může být při nehodě stejně nebezpečná jako nezapnutý pás. S prvními mrazy se do aut vrací péřové bundy a kombinézy – a s nimi i častý problém: pás autosedačky přes tlustou vrstvu oblečení nezajistí dítě tak, jak má.</description></item><item><title>Neúčast v koalici v Liberci je pro ANO zklamáním, v opozici bude po 12 letech</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/902798-neucast-v-koalici-v-liberci-je-pro-ano-zklamanim-v-opozici-bude-po-12.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/902798-neucast-v-koalici-v-liberci-je-pro-ano-zklamanim-v-opozici-bude-po-12.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Neúčast v radniční koalici v Liberci je pro ANO zklamáním. Hnutí o zapojení do koalice usilovalo, řekl lídr ANO Tomáš Rec ČTK. Součástí vedení Liberce bylo ANO posledních 12 let, i když v každém z uplynulých tří volebních období do něj vyslalo jiné zástupce.</description></item><item><title>Ve Svijanech zprovoznili a slavnostně otevřeli rozšířenou varnu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/901024-ve-svijanech-zprovoznili-a-slavnostne-otevreli-rozsirenou-varnu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/901024-ve-svijanech-zprovoznili-a-slavnostne-otevreli-rozsirenou-varnu.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:12:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Pět nových nádob – druhá mladinová pánev, vystírací pánev, rmutovací pánev, scezovací káď a sběrač sladiny – v nové přístavbě rozšířily varnu svijanského pivovaru. Podle historických výkresů je na zakázku pivovaru zhotovila bavorská firma Ziemann.</description></item><item><title>Educa je tady. Startuje dnes, oblíbený veletrh nejen pro studenty začne ve čtvrtek</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/vzdelani/902730-educa-je-tady-startuje-dnes-oblibeny-veletrh-nejen-pro-studenty-zacne-ve-ctvrtek.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/vzdelani/902730-educa-je-tady-startuje-dnes-oblibeny-veletrh-nejen-pro-studenty-zacne-ve-ctvrtek.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Vzdělání</category><description>Jubilejní 20. ročník největšího veletrhu vzdělávání a pracovních příležitostí na severu Čech EDUCA startuje. Liberec i kraj zaplní přednášky, konference a vzdělávací programy pro děti i dospělé. Vše vyvrcholí veletrhem vzdělávání a pracovních příležitostí v Home Credit Areně od 15. do 17. října.</description></item><item><title>V Liberci povládne tříčlenná koalice. ANO míří do opozice</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/902764-v-liberci-povladne-triclenna-koalice-ano-miri-do-opozice.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/902764-v-liberci-povladne-triclenna-koalice-ano-miri-do-opozice.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:36:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Liberec už má dohodu na vládě pro následující čtyři roky. Starostové se dohodli s Lepším Libercem a koalicí Pirátů a Libercem otevřeným lidem (LOL). ANO, které bylo dosud ve vládě, tak míří do opozice. Budoucí trojkoalice nyní jedná o programu a postech.</description></item><item><title>Teploty v dalších dnech porostou. Čeká nás déšť i slunce</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902739-teploty-v-dalsich-dnech-porostou-ceka-nas-dest-i-slunce.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902739-teploty-v-dalsich-dnech-porostou-ceka-nas-dest-i-slunce.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:52:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nový týden přinese do Libereckého kraje pozvolné oteplení, v závěru pracovního týdne se teploty mohou vyšplhat až na osmnáct stupňů. Počasí bude proměnlivé, čekají nás přeháňky, déšť, ale i slunečná obloha.</description></item><item><title>Liberec zrušil zakázku na rozšíření ZŠ Kaplického a neví, kdy ji znovu vypíše</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902688-liberec-zrusil-zakazku-na-rozsireni-zs-kaplickeho-a-nevi-kdy-ji-znovu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902688-liberec-zrusil-zakazku-na-rozsireni-zs-kaplickeho-a-nevi-kdy-ji-znovu.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 06:55:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberec zrušil stavební zakázku na rozšíření ZŠ Kaplického za 145 milionů korun bez DPH. Zatím neví, kdy ji znovu vypíše, rozhodnutí bude na novém vedení města. Důvodů pro zrušení zakázky bylo podle končící náměstkyně primátora Šárky Prachařové (za ANO) víc.</description></item><item><title>Po třech výhrách vyšli naprázdno. Tygři na jihu Čech prohráli 3:4</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/902726-po-trech-vyhrach-vysli-na-prazdno-tygri-v-na-jihu-cech-prohrali-3-4.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/902726-po-trech-vyhrach-vysli-na-prazdno-tygri-v-na-jihu-cech-prohrali-3-4.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 20:25:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Liberečtí hokejisté v desátém extraligovém kole hráli na ledě Motoru České Budějovice. A ve vyrovnaném utkání nakonec tahali za kratší konec, když prohráli těsně 3:4. O výhře rozhodl ve třetí třetině exliberecký Zachar.</description></item></channel></rss>

news.rawText:
výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:22:02 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Horní Podluží – slavnostní předání zásahového vozidla JSDH https://www.vybezek.eu/295716-horni-podluzi-slavnostni-predani-zasahoveho-vozidla-jsdh/ Sat, 10 Oct 2026 14:52:31 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295716 V sobotu 10. října 2026 pod sjezdovkou v Horním Podluží proběhlo slavnostní předání zásahového vozidla místní JSDH.

Za účasti hostů a dalších hasičských jednotek proběhlo slavnostní převzetí automobilu IVECO, který připutoval z Prahy. Dosavadní Tatra se přesune do služby do Národního parku České Švýcarsko.

Že je hasičů stále třeba a že mají práce víc než dost dokazovaly průběžné výjezdy k nedaleké havárii osobního auta u Jiřetína pod Jedlovou či do Varnsdorfu k srnce v korytě Mandavy.

Na technické podrobnosti počkáme na odborníky.

]]> Myšlénky https://www.vybezek.eu/295710-myslenky/ Fri, 09 Oct 2026 17:15:25 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295710 Napadla mne myšlenka. Šílená myšlenka. To se tak člověku bohužel někdy stává…
Řada lidí si asi všimla, že před chozením na akce dávám přednost víc a víc jen chození. To mne totiž tolik nesere, jako potkávání se s lidmi. Původní sem tam zmínka na Výběžku se osamostatnila do zvláštního webu (na který jsem zbyl taky sám) a původní minimnožina (světecké sloupy, křížové cesty, židovské hřbitovy) ještě stále bobtná dalšími speciálně vyčleňovanými kategoriemi (teď jich je 59).

Nenechá mne v klidu žádný divný kámen kolem cesty, je mi líto, o kolika artefaktech a památkách se vlastně vůbec nic neví. Stále smekám před těmi, kteří mi umožní svým úsilím dozvědět se alespoň něco. Pořád jsem na větvi z toho, že já takřka nestíhám jejich výtvory číst a oni museli pátrat, bádat, ověřovat, zkoumat, formulovat a psát a nakonec to v ideálním případě zveřejnit či dokonce vydat. Den každého jednotlivce má zjevně zcela jinou délku. Nicméně jsem rád, že jsou. Na rovinu totiž – tak jako jsem nikdy nebyl a nebudu fotograf, stejně tak nejsem historik, znalec, archivář či kdo ví co ještě. Jsem nejraději, když o tom, co někde vidím, mohu něco okopírovat, opsat.  Od lidí, co vědí, znají, podloženě a oprávněně informují. Mnohdy totiž v odborných textech jsou vedeny spory o architektech či donátorech, ale o lidech tam dole ani slůvko – pokud tedy někde nemají svoji Natálii, která dokáže v archivech dohledat obecní účty a z nich vyčíst nejen třeba jméno kameníka, ale i to, kolik krejcarů dostal kočí za odvoz onoho kamení na stavbu… Já sám cokoli píšu víc než nerad, chybí mi znalosti, pojmy, termíny, a uchyluji se k tomu jen v nouzi nejvyšší.

Jenže prostě někdy visí ve vzduchu otazník a za ním se vznáší myšlenka… V tomhle případě podpořená kombinací různých vlivů. Tedy abych nechodil kolem horké kaše – jde o pomníky. Pomníky padlých Velké války. Nebo tedy spíš o jména na nich. Mám pár knih křížem krážem republikou (většina z nich se tu objevila) a v tomhle ohledu pořád prudce vybočuje série knih Hrobům v dáli, jejíž autorka dokázala o oněch konkrétních lidech vyšťourat i nemožné. A to je právě ono. V evidencích bývá většinou jen popis samotného pomníku, ocitovaných pár jmen, výjimečně něco málo z jejich vojenského života. Postupně ale člověk zjišťuje, kolik se zjistit dá. Pro mne byl velký objev (možná pro mnohé samozřejmost) on-line databáze legionářů. Je tam toho dost, ale doplňovat údaje zpětně k již zveřejněným textům je peklo (ten čas, ten chybějící čas). Ale mnohem víc jich legionáři nebylo… Takže co využít toho, že údajně všechno je dnes digitalizováno a zveřejněno? Obrátil jsem se tedy na dceru, která má s tímhle dost velké zkušenosti z genealogického pátrání. Navedla mne na VHÚ, na projekt Vojenských úmrtních matrik online.

Hele, jako vypadá to skvěle, ohromující čísla, oslavné texty. Jenže jenže… Půlka odkazů v textu nefunguje. Připisuji to peklu neustálého vylepšování a modernizací webů, při nichž část nenávratně vypadne a jiná část dostane zcela jiný link než dřív a veškeré návaznosti se rozpadnou. Nakonec jsem se ale přece jen někam dostal (Digitální studovna Ministerstva obrany ČR). No, a ona již zmíněná ohromující čísla se najednou tak nějak smrskla… Z pár památníků, které jsem prochodil zrovna tenhle týden, totální nechytačka. Komplikovaná tím, že když se něco ukáže, je to německy (což je jazyk, který neovládám) a navíc písmem, které mi dělá potíže číst. Nebo jsou to útržky dokumentů, u nichž absolutně nechápu, co znamenají. Odpíchnout se odtud do skutečných matrik a zjišťovat něco tam, to bude ještě dlouhá cesta. Pokud vůbec průchozí. Zatím jediná nalezená shoda je sice v češtině, ale hned u ní nesouhlasí rok úmrtí. Inu, uvidíme.

Tak o pár dnů později info od dcery:

Zkusila jsem najít nějaké padlé třeba podle pomníku https://www.cokolivokoli.cz/119716-pomnik-obetem-1-svetove-valky-v-kostelci-nad-ohri/

Hledám v databázi padlých https://www.vuapraha.cz/databaze-vha

Podle místa narození Kostelec nad Ohří se našel Krycner Václav (jiný pravopis – KRICNER V., ale to mi nepřijde divné) https://www.vuapraha.cz/padli-1-svetova/83946

má tam rok narození 1889, tak koukám do matrik narozených SOA Litoměřice https://digi.soalitomerice.cz/digitalnibadatelna/ (bohužel litoměřický archiv má nejhorší digitální badatelnu, co jsem zatím viděla, je těžká na ovládání a orientaci) – matrika narozených pro tenhle rok v Kostelci nad Ohří má sign. L10/37

Jeho narození je na snímku 69 – Václav narozený 9. a křtěný 10. ledna 1889, jeho otec Krycner Václav, katol. rolník v Kostelci č. 11, syn Josefa Krycnera chalupníka z Kostelce č. 11 a matky Anny rodem Burešovy z Kostelce č. 11; matka Razáková Marie, katol. dcera Josefa Razáka rolníka z Jarpic č. 26 okres Slané a matky Marie rodem Váňové z Jarpic č. 20

Ale teď koukám, že jeho údaje máš vypsané u pomnínku v Žabovřeskách nad Ohří https://www.cokolivokoli.cz/119574-pomnik-obetem-1-svetove-valky-v-zabovreskach-nad-ohri/
ale nesedí tam věk, dle pomníku mu mělo být 37 let (KRYCNER VÁCLAV 37. R.), tzn. se měl narodit cca 1877-1881.

Hledám potenciální narození jiného V. Krycnera v Žabovřeskách – existuje index pro roky 1840-1913 (sign. L10/E) pro Žabovřesky a okolní obce, koukám na snímky 77-78 (písmeno K, roky 1874-1883) a vidím:
1874 Krycner Václav, otec Václav, 8. 10. Žabovřesky 47, str. 59
1876 Krycner Václav, otec Václav, 14. 12., Kostelec 40, str. 48
1878 Krycner Václav, otec Václav, 17. 3., Žabovřesky 47, str. 65
1878 Krycner Václav, otec Josef, 8. 8., A 50, str. 115
1882 Krycner Václav+, otec Václav, 7. 4., Kostelec, str. 56

Tak se jdu podívat do samotných matrik:

Žabovřesky = sig. L10/40
na snímku 60 (str. 59):
*8. 10. 1874, +20. 1. 1875, Václav Krycner, otec Krycner Václav, matka Brodecká Marie
– ten to být nemůže, zemřel v několika měsících

na snímku 66 (str. 65):
*17. 3. 1878, Václav, Žabovřesky 37, otec Krycner Václav, kat. chalupník ze Žabovřesk, č. 37, syn Václava Krycnera, chalupníka ze Žabovřesk, č. 37, a matky Marie, rodem Faustové z Dušnek, č. 10, okres Roudnice; matka Brodecká Marie, kat. dcera Václava Brodeckého, mlynáře z Velké Kvíce, č. 10. okres Slanský a matky Marie, rodem Martinovské z Řebče č. okres Únhošťský
– ten by to mohl být, není u něj napsané, že by zemřel jako dítě a věkově by to odpovídalo – ale nehledám v matrice zemřelých, jestli taky nezemřel dřív než ve válce, k zápisu o narození se to dopisovalo většinou jen když ten dotyčný umřel brzy po narození a to ne vždy

Kostelec nad Ohří = L10/37
na snímku 50 (str. 48)
*14. 12. 1876, +14. 5. 1878, Václav, otec Krycner Václav, matka Razáková Marie
– ten to být nemůže, zemřel v roce a půl, ale je to starší bratr Václava *1889, kterého jsme identifikovali jako toho, co byl prohlášen za mrtvého v roce 1915

na snímku 58 (str. 56):
*7. 4. 1882, +13. 4. 1882, Václav, otec Krycner Václav, matka Razáková Marie
– ten to být taky nemůže, zemřel po pár dnech – ale zase stejní rodiče

matrika A = sig. L10/25 (obec Budyně nad Ohří)
na snímku 118 (strana 115):
*8. 8. 1878, +24. 8. 1878 Václav, otec Krycner Josef a matka Burešová Marie
– ten to tedy taky být nemůže, ale podle jmen rodičů je to strýc toho padlého Václava *1889… což je teda divné, že by dostal taky jméno Václav, pokud už měl žijícího bratra Václava. To by bylo na další bádání…

Napadlo mě se podívat třeba ještě na svatby, index pro farní obvod má sig. L10/C
koukám na snímek č. 35 a vidím:
1906 Krycner Václav, Lom 66 134 Pokorná Julie B 9

ten zápis je v matrice sign. L10/43 a je to zas úplně jiný Václav, je to na snímku 135:
28. 6. 1906, Lom 352 okres i hejtm. Duchcov, Krycner Václav katol. učitel v Lomu 352, narozen ve Slavětině 50, syn katol. rodičů Jana Krycnera domkáře v Podbradci a matky Anny roz. Beránkové z Řivčic… narozený 16. 10. 1876 ve Slavětíně 50

Dál zkouším hledat „Krycner“ v Národní digitální knihovně https://ndk.cz/ a ne že by nás zajímal ten učitel, ale je zmíněný třeba v Národních listech, rok vydání 1902, ročník 42, datum vydání 2.7.1902, číslo 180, str. 2

ale o „našich“ Václavech jsem nic nenašla.

Dále zkouším sčítání lidu, to je dostupné jen z roku 1921, nejsnadnější je v digitální badatelně SOA Litoměřice zadat název obce a v sekci „Hledá ve vybraných typech záznamů“ zaškrtnout „Operáty“

Žabovřesky 37 (snímky 83-84): bydlí zde Josef Krycner *1872 s manželkou Annou a dětmi
– to vypadá, že by mohl být bratr Václava *1878 – zase by to bylo na další pátrání, aby se to potvrdilo

Kostelec nad Ohří 11 (snímky 29-31): bydlí zde František Krycner *1878 s manželkou a dětmi a bratrem Josefem *1870
– tohle by mohli být bratři Václava *1889, nebo strýcové, nebo třeba bratranci

Matriky zemřelých pro Kostelec ani Žabovřesky nejsou pro roky 1914-1918 digitalizované, třeba by tam mohlo být něco i o prohlášení za mrtvého, nevím.

Takže pár hodin bádání a nic moc z toho. Ale domnívám se, že ti Václavové byli dva, jeden z Kostelce, co je v databázi padlých, a druhý z Žabovřesk, který tam není. Teď mě ale nenapadá, kde by se o nich (na internetu) dalo zjistit něco víc… A takhle nějak by se postupovalo s dalšími vojáky… Co jsem namátkou zkoušela, tak mi to ostatní v té databázi padlých nenašlo. V Kostelci jsem při procházení matriky narazila na různé Šifaldovy, tak by se dalo zjistit třeba něco o té rodině, ale asi nic moc konkrétního… a tak, no.

===

Takže nezbývá než konstatovat, že hafo práce a výsledek nula nula prd. Prostě nápad k ničemu…

]]> Přednáška a netradiční tvoření v Tibetském domě https://www.vybezek.eu/295705-prednaska-a-netradicni-tvoreni-v-tibetskem-dome/ Thu, 08 Oct 2026 18:20:44 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295705 Milí přátelé spolku Thonmi z.s., máme za sebou vydařený filmový večer a na tématiku Tibetu, Tibeťanů, jejich spojení se světem a budování cest navážeme přednáškou, která se uskuteční ve středu 14. října 2026 v 18 hodin opět v Tibetském domě na Asijské poznávací stezce ve Velkém Šenově.

Večerem provede odbornice na Tibet, zakladatelka spolku Thonmi a vědecká pracovnice Orientálního ústavu Akademie věd ČR, Jarmila Ptáčková.

Tibetsko-nepálská hranice vysoko v Himálajích je místem zajímavého dění. Odříznutá od okolního světa vysokými horami, ale i kvůli neexistující infrastruktuře, místo, kde jako by se zastavil čas. Tamní populace patří politicky k Nepálu, kulturně a jazykově jsou to ale spíše Tibeťané. Rozhodně však žijí svým vlastním životem… Alespoň až do nedávna. V posledních letech buduje Čína ze severu hustou infrastrukturu, usilovně opevňuje hranici a zasahuje i do života pohraničních obyvatel. Z jihu se snaží reagovat Nepál a staví těžko sjízdné komunikace, které mají konečně spojit pohraniční oblasti s centrem v Káthmándú. Nové přístupové cesty nabízí průhled do moderního světa a postupně pod hřebeny Himálaje přinášejí nenávratné změny.

Propozice ->

j24hrs_propo

Podle Karla letos asi nejlepší počasí za všech 8 ročníků, cca 180 předem registrovaných. Nicméně: Registrace v místě startu nebudou možné, příchozí se však mohou registrovat na vrcholu Jedlové od 10:30 hod. Těšíme se na vás! Takže kdo chce, může se přidat kdykoli v průběhu až do neděle.

A z loňska mohu beze změny ponechat:

Klobouk dvakrát dolů – před všemi, kdo tuhle akci pořádají a zajišťují (s Karlem v čele), a stejně tak před všemi, kdo dorazí a účastní se (ať už jakkoli dlouho z oněch 24 hodin).

Na FB:

Každý váš krok, výběh i vyšlapaný výškový metr přímo pomáhá handicapovaným dětem a rodinám v našem regionu.

HLAVNÍ NOVINKA LETOŠNÍHO ROČNÍKU:
Nemusíte v tom být sami – letos poprvé můžete vyrazit i v týmech! Dáte dohromady partu z práce, rodinu nebo kamarády a podělíte se o kilometry i skvělé vzpomínky.

Na co se můžete těšit?
* Nezapomenutelná atmosféra v malebném prostředí Jiřetína pod Jedlovou.
* Výzva pro každého – ať už jste zkušený běžec, aktivní turista, nebo chcete jen podpořit dobrou věc volným tempem.
* Skvělá komunita lidí, výborné zázemí a skvělá káva na trati!

Nad ránem:

Dobré ránko z Jedlové. Zatím máme 3434 výstupů a na kontě naskočilo za výstupy 68680,- Kč. Před sebou máme ještě posledních 3,5 hodinky.

Nedělní aktualizace:

Je to tu, dvě a půl hodiny před koncem Jedlová 24 HRS je splněno. Everesting jako první mají za sebou Lenka Hrochová a Dáša Musilová z týmu UL- Trail. Moc gratulujeme a holky hlásí „jdeme dál“.
